sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Gemini CLI is Google's open-source terminal agent for working with code using Gemini models. It is now maintained mainly for organisations using Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise on Google Cloud.
sixtySeconds.problem: Developers want an AI agent in the terminal that can read a large codebase, edit it, debug problems and automate tasks. Gemini CLI does that with Gemini models, MCP servers and a non-interactive mode for scripts.
whoFor: Organisations with Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise
Teams using Code Assist for GitHub on Google Cloud
Developers with paid Gemini API or Vertex AI keys
People scripting codebase questions in CI
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if your organisation has a Gemini Code Assist license. The README says free individual access and Google AI Pro / Ultra moved to Antigravity CLI on June 18, 2026, and Gemini CLI isn't tuned for Gemini 4 models.
requirements: A Gemini Code Assist license, a paid Gemini API key, or Vertex AI access

overview: Gemini CLI is a terminal agent that can query and edit large codebases, build apps from PDFs, images or sketches, debug with natural language, and automate tasks like querying pull requests or handling rebases. MCP servers add capabilities, such as media generation with Imagen, Veo or Lyria.
It can run interactively in your project directory or non-interactively with -p for scripts, with JSON or streaming JSON output. You can include extra directories and choose a model.

The README now points most individuals elsewhere: Antigravity CLI for free and Google AI Pro / Ultra accounts and Gemini 4, and the Gemini API CLI for stateless API commands. Gemini CLI remains for enterprise Code Assist workflows and legacy paid API or Vertex keys. Preview, stable and nightly release channels are published.
